transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-26
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Asteria Head of ML), David Cho (Asteria Platform Lead), Marta Ruiz (Asteria CTO)

Summary: initial implementation orientation, collect integration constraints, agree pilot scope and next steps. medium transcription quality; a few words misheard (e.g., K V cache as K V cash).

Topics covered: onboarding timeline; networking and VPC peering; data residency and retention; pilot scope & success metrics; model selection and cost tradeoffs; security/compliance requirements.

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I'm Samira from Redwood. Uh we'll kick off with quick intros and the objective for today which is to align on integration constraints and define the pilot runway.
00:22 Lina: Hi, I'm Lina, Head of ML at Asteria. We run the customer support NLU stack and want to add generation to assist agents, so latency and data residency are big concerns.
00:40 David: David here, platform lead, I'll be the point on network and infra. We'll need details for V P C peering and IP allow list.
00:50 Marta: Marta, CTO. I'm mostly here to understand timelines and legal/procurement gating.
00:58 Ethan: great, thanks. Quick note: our typical pattern is we can offer hosted API to start then move to Dedicated or Private (V P C / on prem) depending on compliance. we can run a short private trial if needed.
01:20 Lina: Can you explain differences again — like when we'd choose Dedicated vs Private? we've heard both terms.
01:28 Samira: Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with isolation and predictable throughput. Private means customer-managed networking (V P C) or on-prem where the control plane is separate. Private gives you full data residency and K M S/H S M integration. Dedicated is usually faster to get going.
01:55 David: For us, data residency means logs and embeddings must remain in our region; we need audit logs and K M S integration. Is that possible?
02:05 Ethan: yes, we support region pinning and K M S for private deployments, and audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. small caveat: some hosted models cross-region for fallback unless you pin to private mode, which is what many regulated customers do.
02:35 Lina: ok, good. Pilot scope question — we plan to send 10 to 20 concurrent agent queries and peaks to 200 qps in testing. what's our expected latency for generation at that throughput?
02:50 Ethan: depends on model and quantization. For a smaller open model on a dedicated pool we typically see median latencies around 80–120 ms for short prompts, but with higher throughput you'll trade latency for batching efficiency. if you need strict sub-100 ms p95 we can recommend a model and instance class.
03:15 David: Another constraint — our infra team wants to keep egress locked to a set of IPs, and firewall rules won't allow wildcard ranges. we need the exact IPs or egress pattern.
03:28 Samira: We'll provide an allowlist of egress IPs and the ACLs needed. Ethan will follow up with the V P C peering checklist.
03:40 Marta: Procurement-wise, we usually need a statement of work and initial SOW draft to share with legal. how long to produce that?
03:48 Samira: We can get a draft SOW and a pricing summary out in 5 business days after we confirm pilot scope. I'll make that an action item.
04:00 Lina: There's also a question on embedding retention — we don't want PII to be stored. can you do no-retention or opt-out for embeddings?
04:12 Ethan: We have options. Hosted by default may retain telemetry for a limited time for quality. For Private or Dedicated we can configure no retention and ensure embeddings are not stored or are encrypted with your K M S. we'll include the exact retention policies in the security package.
04:35 Lina: Great. also a quick one — do you have S S O? we use Okta.
04:40 Samira: Yes SAML S S O with Okta is supported plus RBAC. we'll include the SSO docs.
04:50 [short crosstalk]
05:10 Ethan: On the technical side, for the pilot we recommend starting with our curated mid-size model (we call it redwood-curie-like), it's cheaper than the largest models and gives high throughput. We'll run a small quantized instance to balance perf and cost.
05:35 David: Are there any pre-reqs for KV cache or prefix caching? we plan to do session-level caching on our side too.
05:44 Ethan: You can do both; Redwood supports prefix/K V cache — though the transcript generator sometimes calls it K V cash — sorry — K V cache. We'll provide guidance on key eviction and cache hits.
06:05 Lina: Who will run the first benchmarks?
06:08 Ethan: We can run an initial baseline on our test cluster if you provide prompt sets and expected token lengths. We'll also give a script to run locally so your infra can validate latency and throughput in your network.
06:25 David: We'll need to test in our staging V P C first. can we do peering to a dedicated pool?
06:32 Samira: Yes, V P C peering to dedicated is supported. For private deployments we can arrange either VPC peering or an on-prem package. We'll share the peering checklist.
06:50 Marta: Legal asks — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs we can share with our legal?
06:58 Samira: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is available, plus we have an ISO self-attestation pack. I'll attach the security package to the runbook.
07:10 Lina: Great. quick note: cost sensitivity — our finance wants a rough per-1k-token ballpark for the curated model vs large LLM so they can budget.
07:22 Samira: We'll include pricing tiers in the summary. For the pilot we can give estimated monthly spend based on your throughput numbers.
07:30 [pause]
07:48 Ethan: For rollout strategy — we usually do a canary for 10% of traffic for 2 weeks, then ramp to 50% if metrics look good. That helps catch regressions.
08:05 David: Metrics to monitor for us: p95 latency, error rate, token cost, and regression in generation quality measured by a small eval set.
08:18 Lina: We'll prepare an eval set. what's the recommended size?
08:22 Ethan: 200 to 500 representative prompts is a good start. We'll also suggest an automatic regression alert tied to that eval set.
08:35 Samira: Ok, to summarize the high-level timeline: 1) runbook and SOW draft in ~5 business days; 2) network deep-dive with Ethan week of 2026-03-01; 3) Asteria shares prompts and throughput targets by 2026-03-05; 4) pilot kickoff the week of 2026-03-08 assuming network and credentials are in place.
09:00 Marta: That timeline sounds feasible. procurement target is end of March, so aligning pilot before end of March is ideal.
09:12 [interruption — connection briefly drops; filler noises]
09:45 Lina: also wondering about model version pinning — if you upgrade models, can we pin?
09:50 Ethan: yes, we support model version pinning and canary rollouts. We'll explain the rollback/fallback policies.
10:05 David: For audit logging — does the platform produce request-level logs or token-level logs we can ingest?
10:12 Samira: We provide request metadata, anonymized tokens in hosted mode unless you opt out. For Private, full audit logs can be delivered to your SIEM. We'll include the exact fields in the security doc.
10:30 Lina: Ok, next steps on our side: we'll get the prompt set and network diagrams to Ethan and David will coordinate firewall details. Marta will loop in procurement/legal.
10:45 Samira: Perfect. We'll capture these as action items and follow up. Any other questions?
11:00 Lina: Nothing else right now. Thanks.
11:05 Marta: no, thanks.
11:10 [wrap up]
11:20 Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll send the runbook and security pack and schedule the network deep-dive. expect Samira email with links and Ethan will reach out on calendar invites.

End of transcript.
